note_on_sourcing: Official = stanford.edu / admission.stanford.edu / facts.stanford.edu / gostanford.com (Stanford-published). Common Data Set (CDS) is Stanford's own annual filing but was read here via third-party summaries; direct PDF: https://irds.stanford.edu/data-findings/cds. Inferred = third-party analytics / former-AO accounts / advocacy. Where a claim could not be verified against a Stanford-published source it is marked 待核实.

official.dimension: 学术硬指标-必修申请材料
official.finding: Required first-year components: Common Application; $100 fee (or waiver); ACT or SAT scores; School Report form + counselor letter; official transcript(s); midyear transcript (due Feb 15); 2 teacher letters of recommendation. Optional: arts portfolio.

ACT or SAT is REQUIRED for first-year and transfer applicants beginning with the Fall 2026 entry term. No minimum score; no score guarantees admission. Self-reported scores accepted for review; official scores required only if enrolling. Stanford superscores both SAT (EBRW+Math) and ACT, and accepts both original and redesigned ACT.
Last acceptable ACT: September (REA) / December (RD). Last acceptable SAT: October (REA) / December (RD). Application deadlines: REA Nov 1, RD Jan 5.

English-proficiency tests (TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo) are NOT a required application component, and 'English Proficiency tests cannot be used as a substitute for the ACT/SAT requirement.' Fluency is expected and may be evidenced elsewhere; exam results are 'useful' but not mandatory for undergrad.

official.dimension: 学术硬指标-GPA与课程难度
official.finding: 'The primary criterion for admission to Stanford is academic excellence, which means flawless or nearly flawless grades in rigorous courses.' Stanford does NOT set a minimum GPA and does NOT require a specific number of AP/honors courses, but 'the strongest applicants will present outstanding results in a rigorous program of study.' Grade 9 is treated as a transition year; review focuses on grades 10, 11 and final year.

Recommended (not required) HS curriculum: English 4 yrs (writing/literature); Math 4 yrs incl. calculus; History/Social Studies min 3 yrs; Science min 3 yrs (bio/chem/physics/CS etc.); World Language min 3 yrs of the same language. Aim ~5 academic courses per semester, including senior year.

AP exams not mandatory, BUT if any AP taken, ALL AP scores must be self-reported. IB Diploma students outside the US must submit predicted IB marks (incl. TOK/essay bonus). British-system applicants must submit GCSE results + predicted A-Level marks; generally at least three full A-Level courses.

official.dimension: 学术硬指标-CDS录取数据(2025-26, Class of 2029)
official.finding: 60,646 applicants; 2,302 admitted (3.80%); 1,839 enrolled. SAT middle 50% 1520-1570; ACT middle 50% 34-36. (Stanford's own CDS, Section C1/C9-C11.)

official.dimension: 学术硬指标-CDS录取数据(2024-25, Class of 2028)
official.finding: 57,326 applicants; 2,067 admitted (3.61%); 1,693 enrolled. Average unweighted HS GPA 3.94; 73.3% presented a 4.0 unweighted GPA; 97.8% in top 10% of class, 100% top 25%. 50.3% submitted SAT, 19% submitted ACT (test-optional year). (Stanford CDS 2024-25.)

official.dimension: 软技能与价值观-C7权重表
official.finding: CDS Section C7 factor ratings. VERY IMPORTANT: rigor of secondary school record; academic GPA; application essay; recommendation(s); extracurricular activities; talent/ability; character/personal qualities. CONSIDERED: standardized test scores; class rank; interview; first-generation status; alumni relation; geographic residence; volunteer work; work experience. NOT CONSIDERED: state residency; religious affiliation/commitment; level of applicant's interest (demonstrated interest). (Ratings shift slightly by edition; verify current PDF.)

Official admissions language centers on INTELLECTUAL VITALITY, not on entrepreneurship or business outcomes. 'Stanford students are brimming with curiosity, openness, and imagination... a building cornerstone dedicated to the things that haven't happened yet and the people who are about to dream them up.' Stanford looks for how applicants 'expanded your perspective and sought new opportunities.' No official statement ranks practice/startups above theory; the rubric rewards curiosity-driven pursuit, in and out of the classroom.

official.dimension: 软技能与价值观-课外与影响力
official.finding: 'An exceptional depth of experience in one or two activities may demonstrate your passion more than minimal participation in five or six clubs.' Work and family responsibilities count. 'In general, we want to understand the impact you have had at your job, in your family, in your school, and in the larger community.'

official.dimension: 软技能与价值观-情境审查
official.finding: Stanford reviews achievement 'in context': background, educational pathway, and work/family responsibilities; evaluates how you excelled with what your school/community made available. No preference stated for a particular school type.
Stanford Questions = 5 Short Questions (3-word min / 50-word max each) + 3 Short Essays (100-250 words each). See docs.supplements for exact prompts.

'There are no right or wrong answers and you should allow your genuine voice to come through. These questions help us get to know you as a friend, future roommate, and classmate.' Applicants apply to the university as a whole, not a major/school.

Alumni interview is OPTIONAL and extends only where alumni are available; many applicants receive none. Declining or opting out carries no penalty and the application is complete with or without an interview. If held, the alumni volunteer writes a report that becomes part of the admission file.

Stanford fields Men's Rowing, Women's Rowing, and Women's Lightweight Rowing as varsity programs with official walk-on pathways. Official recruiting process: complete the online recruiting questionnaire; email coaches with rowing/erging video, unofficial test scores and transcripts; register with the NCAA Eligibility Center (Clearinghouse). NCAA contact rules: coaches may email/call after June 15 between sophomore and junior year; official visits permitted after Aug 1 between sophomore and junior year (max 5 official visits, 1 per institution).

'In some cases, exceptional abilities in athletics may influence our decision if the applicant is otherwise well-qualified, but such abilities never, by themselves, ensure admission to Stanford.' (This is Stanford's only published statement on athletic weight.)

Officially NOT considered: demonstrated interest (level of applicant's interest), state residency, religious affiliation. There is no 'Why Stanford?' essay. Legacy is not a stated factor (Stanford opted out of California's legacy-reporting grant for the Class of 2029).

Enrolled 1,866 first-years. 20% first-generation. HS type: 58% public, 28% private, 14% international, <1% home school. From 50 US states + 64 non-US countries. Self-reported ethnicity: Asian 35%, White 25%, International 13%, Hispanic 12%, Two or more 10%, Black 4%, <1% AI/AN, <1% NHPI. Gender: 52% men / 48% women.

stanford.edu: 'There's no secret formula for admission to Stanford... we look for students who are curious and questioning, who are driven to explore, and who commit themselves deeply to opportunities for learning and growth.' Tuition free for families with income under $150k (typical assets); need-based aid for 70%+ of admits.

inferred.finding: Despite 'no minimum,' the enrolled distribution implies practical expectations: ~97-98% of admits are in the top 10% of their HS class and ~73% hold an unweighted 4.0; a 3.9+ unweighted GPA in the most demanding available courses (typically 8-12+ AP/IB/dual-enrollment courses) is the de facto norm.
inferred.basis: CDS 2024-25 C11 distribution + collegevine/College Transitions analysis

inferred.finding: For the Class of 2030 (first test-required cycle) competitive applicants should target roughly SAT 1520-1570+/ACT 34-36; the pre-2026 middle 50% (1510-1570 SAT) is a floor guide, likely to tighten or hold once scores are mandatory for everyone.
inferred.basis: CDS ranges (test-optional, self-selected submitters) + unive.ai / cosmic.nyc projections

inferred.finding: Practical/impact-driven work (independent projects, original research, community initiatives, ventures) is treated as EVIDENCE of intellectual vitality rather than an end in itself. Stanford rewards students who turn curiosity into action 'beyond what a course requires'; visible real-world impact strengthens the file but is not an officially stated preference over theoretical depth. Depth + a genuine spike outweighs a generic activity list.
inferred.basis: admission.stanford.edu IV language + multiple former-AO accounts (novascholar, koppelmangroup, gomdori)

inferred.dimension: 软技能与价值观-Intellectual Vitality为独立评级
inferred.finding: Former Stanford AOs report that Stanford, unlike the Ivies, maintains a SEPARATE 'intellectual vitality' rating; a top academic rating paired with low IV is a documented rejection pattern. Essays (esp. the IV short essay) and teacher recommendations are the main evidence surfaces.
inferred.basis: Novascholar interview with former Stanford AO Dr. Irena Smith; chance-me.ai / gomdorieducation analyses

inferred.finding: Dean of Admission Richard Shaw (since 2005) is widely quoted: 'It's a holistic evaluation... we're also looking for evidence that this young person has a passion... We want to hear a voice—that's a critical component.' Polished/AI-sounding prose is flagged as inauthentic.
inferred.basis: Multiple third-party quotes of Shaw; not located verbatim on an admission.stanford.edu page

inferred.finding: The 3 essays map to: (1) Intellectual Vivality — show HOW you pursue an idea on your own time, not a credential; (2) Roommate note — reveal personality/how you relate to others, not a second resume; (3) Distinctive contribution — name something specific you'd bring, the closest thing to a 'Why Stanford.' Short answers (50 words) are a deliberate compression test of voice; 'safe' generic answers weaken the IV dimension.
inferred.basis: admission.stanford.edu prompt text + college transitions / chance-me / novascholar strategy analyses

inferred.finding: Interview carries low weight (CDS: 'Considered'). Interview capacity is alumni-limited, so it functions mainly as a tie-breaker/verification of voice rather than a deciding factor; not being offered one is neutral.

inferred.dimension: 潜规则-录取者画像反推
inferred.finding: Patterns from admitted-student profiles (Stanford Daily, Class of 2029): interdisciplinary double majors, student-body/advocacy leadership (national student councils, UNICEF advisory groups), self-founded STEM/education initiatives, and 'pursued a passion for its own sake.' Interdisciplinary/entrepreneurial framing and concrete community impact recur; pure credential stacking does not.
inferred.basis: stanforddaily.com Class of 2029 features + official class profile

inferred.finding: Admission is not a stat threshold with essays attached: ~27% of enrolled admits did NOT have a 4.0, so a strong-but-not-perfect GPA with brutal rigor is inside the distribution. Demonstrated interest and legacy do not move the needle (officially Not Considered / not reported).
inferred.basis: CDS 2024-25 C7 + C11 distribution analysis (unive.ai, classeva)

inferred.finding: No official erg threshold is published by Stanford. Third-party benchmarks: Men's heavyweight 2k ~6:15-6:30 = solid D1 interest, sub-6:15 = priority recruit; Women's openweight sub-7:00-7:10 priority; Women's lightweight sub-7:35 (130 lb cap). Male rowers typically get NO athletic scholarship (need-based aid only); Women's rowing (NCAA D1) can offer athletic aid. A recruited athlete still passes the full academic review; coach advocacy only matters if the applicant is 'otherwise well-qualified.'
inferred.basis: NCAA/IRA recruiting guides (NCSA, roweracademy, vincekotchian, crewconnection) + The Rowing Association Stanford men's Class of 2029 notes

inferred.finding: Stanford men's rowing recruited ~9 athletes for Fall '26; most recruited rowers come with strong junior national-team pedigree OR elite ergs, and are selected on 'character, athletic ability, and academic aptitude.' A competitive-but-not-elite HS rower (e.g. erg in the mid-7:xx range) is far more likely to enter via the walk-on/novice pathway (fall-quarter tryout) than via a recruiting slot. This is the realistic route for an academically strong non-national-team oarsman.
inferred.basis: The Rowing Association Fall '25 coaches report quoting Stanford men's coach; gostanford walk-on FAQ

supplements.prompt: Short Q1: What is the most significant challenge that society faces today?
Short Q2: How did you spend your last two summers?
Short Q3: What historical moment or event do you wish you could have witnessed?
Short Q4: Briefly elaborate on one of your extracurricular activities, a job you hold, or responsibilities you have for your family.
Short Q5: List five things that are important to you.

Essay 1 (Intellectual Vitality): The Stanford community is deeply curious and driven to learn in and out of the classroom. Reflect on an idea or experience that makes you genuinely excited about learning.

Essay 2 (Roommate note): Virtually all of Stanford's undergraduates live on campus. Write a note to your future roommate that reveals something about you or that will help your roommate—and us—get to know you better.

Essay 3 (Distinctive contribution): Please describe what aspects of your life experiences, interests, and character would help you make a distinctive contribution as an undergraduate to Stanford University.

docs.interview: Optional alumni interview; extended only where alumni are available and only to applicants whose high school is in an interview area; many applicants are not offered one. Declining or opting out incurs no penalty and the file is complete with or without it. The alumni volunteer submits a report that becomes part of the admission file. (Source: https://admission.stanford.edu/apply/first-year/interview.html)

myths.claim: You must be a genius with perfect test scores (e.g. 1580+ SAT) to get in.
myths.reality: Stanford publishes NO minimum score and rates test scores BELOW rigor/GPA/essays/recommendations/character in its own CDS; ~27% of enrolled admits did not have a 4.0 GPA. Test scores are a threshold/context signal, not the differentiator.

myths.claim: You need a published research paper or a startup to have a chance.
myths.reality: Neither is required or stated as a criterion. Stanford evaluates intellectual vitality and impact in context; self-directed depth in one or two activities is explicitly valued over a long activity list.

myths.claim: Visiting campus / emailing admissions / opening the portal (demonstrated interest) helps.
myths.reality: Level of applicant's interest is officially NOT CONSIDERED. Demonstrated interest has zero weight.

Alumni relation is only 'Considered' (not Very Important) in the CDS, and Stanford's Class of 2029 was the first after Stanford opted out of California's legacy-admission reporting grant; no legacy preference is published.

myths.claim: A hyper-polished, professional-sounding essay is best.
myths.reality: Official guidance asks for 'your genuine voice'; AOs report flagging AI-polished/inauthentic prose. Voice, specificity and self-revelation are rewarded over polish.

myths.claim: Being a recruited rower guarantees admission.
myths.reality: Official: athletic ability 'never, by themselves, ensure admission.' Recruitment only helps if the applicant is 'otherwise well-qualified'; the full academic review still applies.

rowing_vs_admissions.level: Stanford fields three varsity rowing programs: Men's Rowing (openweight, IRA-governed, no athletic scholarships — need-based aid), Women's Rowing (NCAA D1, athletic aid possible), and Women's Lightweight Rowing (130 lb cap). Official walk-on/novice tryout pathway exists for all (fall-quarter tryouts). Recruiting route requires the online recruiting questionnaire, coach email with video/erg/scores/transcripts, and NCAA Eligibility Center registration.
rowing_vs_admissions.impact: Official: 'exceptional abilities in athletics may influence our decision if the applicant is otherwise well-qualified, but such abilities never, by themselves, ensure admission.' Recruited athletes are reviewed as part of the holistic whole via coach advocacy; the academic bar (rigor + GPA + essays) still applies. No official erg threshold is published; third-party benchmarks put men's heavyweight D1 interest around a 2k of ~6:15-6:30 (sub-6:15 = priority recruit) and priority women's openweight around sub-7:00-7:10. Realistically, a strong student who is a competitive-but-not-national-team HS rower is best served by the walk-on/novice pathway plus a strong academic profile, rather than expecting a recruiting slot.
